description: This line plot illustrates the performance of three different trigger insertion strategies—labeled 'start', 'random', and 'end'—on the SST-2 dataset with a clean-label poison rate of 5%, as measured by ASR (Attack Success Rate) on the vertical axis, which ranges from 0.2 to 0.9 in linear scale. The horizontal axis lists trigger words—'bb', 'mb', 'cf', 'beautiful', 'excellent', 'gorgeous', 'wonderful', 'brilliant', 'stunning', 'beautifully'—arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model. The 'start' strategy is represented by a teal line with circle markers, beginning at an ASR of 0.2 and rising to a peak of 0.91 at 'stunning', then slightly declining to 0.89 at 'beautifully'. The 'random' strategy is shown as an orange line with 'x' markers, starting at 0.52, dipping to a low of 0.2 at 'cf', then rising to 0.89 at 'stunning' before ending at 0.91 at 'beautifully'. The 'end' strategy is depicted by a purple line with circle markers, beginning at 0.51, rising to a peak of 0.88 at 'gorgeous', then declining to 0.67 at 'brilliant', and ending at 0.87 at 'beautifully'. All three lines show generally increasing ASR as the trigger word moves rightward along the axis, with the 'start' and 'random' strategies reaching similar high ASR values at the end of the sequence.
